{{Short description|Swiss climate scientist and professor}}
{{Expand German|date=September 2026}}
[[File:ETH-BIB-Knutti, Reto (1973-)-Portr 17403.jpg|thumb|Knutti in 2017]]

'''Reto Knutti''' (born 1973) is a Swiss climate scientist and professor of climate physics at [[ETH Zurich]]'s [[Institute for Atmospheric and Climate Science]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2016/07/eight-professors-appointed-at-eth-zurich.html | title=Eight professors appointed at ETH Zurich | work=ETH Zurich | date=15 July 2016 | accessdate=19 April 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.iac.ethz.ch/people-iac/person-detail.html?persid=146272 | title=Reto Knutti | publisher=ETH Zurich | work=Institute for Atmospheric and Climate Science | accessdate=19 April 2017}}</ref> He is known for his research involving [[climate model]]s,<ref>{{cite journal | url=http://www.nature.com/news/cloud-seeding-surprise-could-improve-climate-predictions-1.19971 | title=Cloud-seeding surprise could improve climate predictions | journal=Nature | date=25 May 2016 | accessdate=19 April 2017 | author=Castelvecchi, Davide| doi=10.1038/nature.2016.19971 | s2cid=131886145 | url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://newrepublic.com/article/141000/can-world-beat-climate-change-without-us | title=Can the World Beat Climate Change Without the U.S.? | magazine=The New Republic | date=28 February 2017 | accessdate=19 April 2017 | author=Rabinowitz, Abby}}</ref> and has been a key member of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/10/08/science/how-to-slice-a-global-carbon-pie.html | title=How to Slice a Global Carbon Pie? | work=The New York Times | date=8 October 2013 | accessdate=19 April 2017 | author=Gillis, Justin}}</ref>
